subject: Close runway: Anchored replan & staggered go-live commitments
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@medpliance.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@medpliance.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & go-live window for Q4

Hi Grace —

Quick update from our side: the security/compliance review for the ML score export is taking longer than we anticipated. The SSO and vendor risk team have flagged two items (encryption-at-rest proof & a narrower data-retention clause) and want an additional review cycle. That pushes our procurement signoff out about ~2 weeks.

Given that, we'd like to propose a staggered launch: surface-level reporting (read-only dashboards) first, then enable model scoring once we clear the compliance checklist. I attached an updated MAP (Medpliance_MAP_v3.xlsx) and a proposed procurement timeline (procurement-timeline.pdf) for your reference.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood accommodate a canary/reporting-first go-live while model scoring remains behind a feature flag?
- If acceptance slips, can we document a credit or milestone-based payment hold in the MAP so procurement can justify the schedule change to finance?

Appreciate a quick read — would like to confirm a revised target by end of this week if possible.

Thanks,
Alicia Torres
Director, Procurement — Medpliance

Attachments: Medpliance_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), procurement-timeline.pdf (PDF)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@medpliance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & go-live window for Q4

Alicia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the MAP + timeline. We can absolutely work with a staggered approach; that aligns with what we've done for other customers to reduce risk while procurement finishes reviews.

Proposal (quick):
- Anchor the MAP with two visible windows: Reporting Canary (read-only dashboards) targeted for the current window + Model Score Rollout targeted 3 weeks later. That three-week buffer gives us room to absorb the compliance review without rebooking infra.
- Redwood will enable a feature-flagged scoring endpoint for the canary so you can validate UI/workflow without production scoring.
- If procurement acceptance slips beyond 30 days, we can bake a conditional credit into the MAP (Ben, Marissa — can you confirm the right credit language and limits?).

Next steps from our side:
1) Ben to confirm dedicated/burst capacity options and estimate the incremental cost for a staggered canary.
2) Jordan will produce a short escalation note for our Customer Success playbook so we keep timeline owners aligned.
3) I will update the MAP spreadsheet with milestone owners and send a formal version for signature (DocuSign link to follow) — can you confirm the procurement milestone dates in the attached timeline?

Proposed sync: Thu, Nov 13 at 10:00 PT for an executive-level alignment (30 min). If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment (referenced): Medpliance_MAP_v3.xlsx (updated anchor rows)

> On Wed, Nov 5, 2025 at 09:12 AM Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@medpliance.com> wrote:
> Hi Grace —
> 
> Quick update from our side: the security/compliance review...

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & go-live window for Q4

Grace / Jordan —

I reviewed the MAP and the staggered approach looks workable from capacity & SRE planning. Notes:

- Capacity: We can reserve a Dedicated burst (2 x A40-equivalent nodes) for the Reporting Canary in the requested window, then transition model scoring to shared capacity once procurement clears. That limits cost delta to roughly +12% for the month of Dec versus the baseline.
- SLA/credits: We can include a conditional credit clause in the MAP: if acceptance (final scoring enablement) is delayed >30 days from the originally agreed acceptance date, Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to 20% of the monthly dedicated cost for the impacted month. Marissa — please validate wording and legal constraints.
- Fallback: If you need scoring in a constrained window, we can temporarily pin an earlier, quantized model variant to reduce memory footprint and accelerate rollout; quality trade-offs documented in the MAP.

I'll draft a short addendum with the two capacity options (reserved burst vs. pay-as-you-go surge) and the proposed credit language. Grace — once you update the MAP with milestone owners, send it to me for the cost appendix.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: capacity_estimate_dec.pdf (will attach in next email)

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@medpliance.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@medpliance.com>, procurement@medpliance.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & go-live window for Q4

Grace —

Thanks, that path looks good. Procurement milestone confirmations below:
- SSO/identity review complete: 2025-11-20
- SOC2 evidence and legal review: 2025-11-27
- Final procurement sign-off: 2025-12-03 (target)

We accept the staggered plan: Reporting Canary first, followed by scoring enablement. Procurement requests the MAP include: milestone owners, the conditional credit clause you described, and a short rollback/fallback acceptance test (30-minute smoke test) for the scoring endpoint.

Please send the updated MAP with milestone owners and the DocuSign link for signature. If possible, keep the canary start no earlier than Nov 26 to ensure SSO is provisioned.

Tom (copied) will coordinate SSO next steps; procurement@ is the distribution list for any contract redlines.

Thanks —
Alicia Torres
Director, Procurement — Medpliance
